   151	def diff_text(report: dict) -> str:
   152	    out = [f"diff {report['old']} → {report['new']}"]
   153	    out.append(f" IDs added {len(report['added'])}, removed {len(report['removed'])}, changed {len(report['changed'])}")
   154	    for item in report["added"]:
   155	        history = f" — already in this file's history (last changed in {item['seen_in_history']}): check it is not a reused retired ID" \
   156	            if "seen_in_history" in item else ""
   157	        out.append(f"  + {item['id']} at {item['at']}{history}")
   158	    if report.get("history", {}).get("unchecked"):
   159	        out.append(f"  note: history not checked for {report['history']['unchecked']} added ID(s) beyond the first {HISTORY_LIMIT}")
   160	    for item in report["removed"]:
   161	        cited = f"; still cited at {', '.join(item['still_cited'])}" if item["still_cited"] else ""
   162	        out.append(f"  - {item['id']} (was {item['was']}){cited}")
   163	    by_file: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   164	    for item in report["changed"]:
   165	        old_path, _, old_lines = item["old"].rpartition(":")
   166	        new_path, _, new_lines = item["new"].rpartition(":")
   167	        moved = "" if old_path == new_path else f" (moved from {old_path})"
   168	        by_file[new_path].append(f"{item['id']} {old_lines}→{new_lines}{moved}")
   169	    for path, entries in sorted(by_file.items()):
   170	        out.append(f"  ~ {path}: " + "; ".join(entries))
   171	    for p in report["positional"]:
   172	        out.append(f" positional {p['parent']}: {p['old_count']} → {p['new_count']} item(s), {p['kind']}")
   173	        for item in p["items"]:
   174	            cited = f" — cited at {', '.join(item['cited_at'])}" if item["cited_at"] else ""
   175	            out.append(f"   {item['id']}: was “{item['old']}” now “{item['new']}”{cited}")
   176	    out.append(f" sections changed {len(report['sections'])}")
   177	    for s in report["sections"][:60]:
   178	        out.append(f"  {s['state']:7} {s['section']}")
   179	    if len(report["sections"]) > 60:
   180	        out.append(f"  … {len(report['sections']) - 60} more")
   181	    return "\n".join(out)

   348	        nonblank = {n for n in range(start, end + 1) if n <= len(lines) and lines[n - 1].strip()}
   349	        if not historical & nonblank:
   350	            return "current"
   351	        return "historical" if nonblank <= historical else "partly historical"
   352	
   353	    def _unit_at(self, path: str, line: int) -> Hit:
   354	        row = self.conn.execute(
   355	            "SELECT sid FROM spans WHERE path=? AND start<=? AND end>=? AND kind IN ('row','item','para','yaml','section') "
   356	            "ORDER BY CASE kind WHEN 'row' THEN 0 WHEN 'yaml' THEN 1 WHEN 'item' THEN 2 WHEN 'para' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END, (end-start) LIMIT 1",
   357	            (path, line, line)).fetchone()
   358	        if not row:
   359	            return self._range_hit(path, line, line)
   360	        return self.hit_from_span(row["sid"])
   361	
   362	    def _headings(self, text: str, paths: list[str], notes: list[str]) -> list[Hit]:
   363	        needle = text.strip().lower()
   364	        rows = self.conn.execute(
   365	            "SELECT sid, path, title FROM spans WHERE kind='section' AND path IN (%s)" % ",".join("?" * len(paths)), paths).fetchall()
   366	        exact = [r for r in rows if r["title"].lower() == needle]
   367	        prefix = [r for r in rows if r["title"].lower().startswith(needle)]
   368	        contains = [r for r in rows if needle in r["title"].lower()]
   369	        chosen = exact or prefix or contains
   370	        if len(chosen) > 1:
   371	            notes.append(f"{len(chosen)} headings match {text!r}; showing all")
   372	        return [self.hit_from_span(r["sid"]) for r in chosen]

1	"""BMAD preview ticket tree adapter (read-only).
     2	
     3	A container is a `<type>-<slug>/` folder with a same-named file and a
     4	`tickets.toml`; initiatives list `[[epic]]`, epics list `[[entry]]`. Each
     5	container's requirement source is, in order: its own `## Requirements` section,
     6	a referenced numbered source (a `prd —` or `spec —` References line), or a
     7	`spec-*/SPEC.md` in its folder. BMAD's tickets.py never validates `covers`;
     8	this module does, without changing anything.
     9	"""
    10	from __future__ import annotations
    11	
    12	import json
    13	import posixpath
    14	import re
    15	import tomllib
    16	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    17	
    18	from .queries import Queries
    19	
    20	REQUIREMENT_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(?:\*\*)?(?P<id>[A-Z][A-Za-z]*-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?:\*\*)?(?:\s*\((?P<parent>[^)]*)\))?")
    21	REFERENCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(?P<type>[a-z][\w-]*)\s+—\s+(?P<location>[^,\s]+)")
    22	NUMBERED_SOURCE_TYPES = ("prd", "spec")
    23	
    24	
    25	@dataclass(slots=True)
    26	class Ticket:
    27	    ref: str                  # "<epic id>.<entry id>" or the epic id
    28	    container: str            # folder of the owning container
    29	    title: str
    30	    covers: list[str]
    31	    toml_path: str
    32	    file: str | None = None   # pulled leaf file, which is the truth over tickets.toml content fields
    33	    file_covers: list[str] | None = None
    34	    status: str | None = None
    35	
    36	    @property
    37	    def planned(self) -> bool:
    38	        """A leaf with neither a file nor a plan yet: expected work, not a defect."""
    39	        return "." in self.ref and self.file is None and self.status is None
    40	
    41	
    42	@dataclass(slots=True)
    43	class Container:
    44	    folder: str
    45	    kind: str                 # initiative | epic
    46	    file: str | None
    47	    toml_path: str
    48	    covers: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    49	    requirements: dict[str, tuple[str | None, int]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    50	    sources: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    51	    parent: str | None = None
    52	    epic_id: str | None = None
    53	
    54	
    55	@dataclass(slots=True)
    56	class Chain:
    57	    ticket: str
    58	    covered_id: str
    59	    state: str                # resolved | unresolved | not-in-container-covers | upstream-unresolved
    60	    target: str | None        # the population ID the chain reaches (e.g. FR-7)
    61	    detail: str
    62	
    63	
    64	@dataclass(slots=True)
    65	class Tree:
    66	    containers: dict[str, Container] = field(default_factory=dict)
    67	    tickets: list[Ticket] = field(default_factory=list)
    68	    problems: list[tuple[str, str, int, str]] = field(default_factory=list)  # code, path, line, detail
    69	
    70	
    71	def load_tree(q: Queries) -> Tree:
    72	    tree = Tree()
    73	    tomls = sorted(p for p, f in q.files.items() if f["artifact"] == "tickets-toml")
    74	    for path in tomls:
    75	        try:
    76	            data = tomllib.loads("\n".join(q.lines(path)))
    77	        except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as error:
    78	            tree.problems.append(("ticket-toml-invalid", path, 0, str(error)))
    79	            continue
    80	        folder = posixpath.dirname(path)
    81	        name = posixpath.basename(folder)
    82	        kind = "initiative" if "epic" in data else "epic"
    83	        file = f"{folder}/{name}.md"
    84	        container = Container(folder, kind, file if file in q.files else None, path)
    85	        if container.file:
    86	            _read_container_file(q, container)
    87	        tree.containers[folder] = container
    88	        if kind == "initiative":
    89	            for epic in data.get("epic", []):
    90	                epic_folder = f"{folder}/{epic.get('slug', '')}"
    91	                tree.tickets.append(Ticket(str(epic.get("id")), folder, epic.get("title", ""), list(epic.get("covers", [])), path))
    92	                tree.containers.setdefault(epic_folder, Container(epic_folder, "epic", None, "", parent=folder))
    93	                tree.containers[epic_folder].epic_id = str(epic.get("id"))
    94	                tree.containers[epic_folder].parent = folder
    95	    for folder, container in tree.containers.items():
    96	        if container.kind != "epic" or not container.toml_path:
    97	            continue
    98	        data = tomllib.loads("\n".join(q.lines(container.toml_path)))
    99	        parent = posixpath.dirname(folder)
   100	        container.parent = container.parent or (parent if parent in tree.containers else None)
   101	        leaves = _leaf_files(q, folder)
   102	        for entry in data.get("entry", []):
   103	            ident = str(entry.get("id"))
   104	            ref = f"{container.epic_id}.{ident}" if container.epic_id else ident
   105	            ticket = Ticket(ref, folder, entry.get("title", ""), list(entry.get("covers", [])), container.toml_path)
   106	            leaf = leaves.get(ident)
   107	            if leaf:
   108	                ticket.file, ticket.file_covers = leaf
   109	            ticket.status = _plan_status(q, folder, ident)
   110	            tree.tickets.append(ticket)
   111	    return tree
   112	
   113	
   114	def _read_container_file(q: Queries, container: Container) -> None:
   115	    row = q.conn.execute("SELECT frontmatter FROM files WHERE path=?", (container.file,)).fetchone()
   116	    frontmatter = json.loads(row["frontmatter"]) if row and row["frontmatter"] else {}
   117	    covers = frontmatter.get("covers")
   118	    container.covers = list(covers) if isinstance(covers, list) else []
   119	    lines = q.lines(container.file)
   120	    section = None
   121	    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
   122	        if line.startswith("## "):
   123	            section = line[3:].strip().lower()
   124	            continue
   125	        if section == "requirements":
   126	            match = REQUIREMENT_LINE.match(line)
   127	            if match:
   128	                container.requirements[match.group("id")] = (match.group("parent").strip() if match.group("parent") else None, number)
   129	        elif section == "references":
   130	            match = REFERENCE_LINE.match(line)
   131	            if match and match.group("type") in NUMBERED_SOURCE_TYPES:
   132	                container.sources.append(match.group("location").strip("`"))
   133	
   134	
   135	def _leaf_files(q: Queries, folder: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, list[str]]]:
   136	    leaves = {}
   137	    for path, info in q.files.items():
   138	        if info["artifact"] != "ticket-leaf" or posixpath.dirname(path) != folder:
   139	            continue
   140	        row = q.conn.execute("SELECT frontmatter FROM files WHERE path=?", (path,)).fetchone()
   141	        frontmatter = json.loads(row["frontmatter"]) if row and row["frontmatter"] else {}
   142	        if "id" in frontmatter:
   143	            covers = frontmatter.get("covers")
   144	            leaves[str(frontmatter["id"])] = (path, list(covers) if isinstance(covers, list) else [])
   145	    return leaves
   146	
   147	
   148	def _plan_status(q: Queries, folder: str, ident: str) -> str | None:
   149	    for path, info in q.files.items():
   150	        if info["artifact"] != "ticket-plan" or posixpath.dirname(path) != folder:
   151	            continue
   152	        row = q.conn.execute("SELECT frontmatter FROM files WHERE path=?", (path,)).fetchone()
   153	        frontmatter = json.loads(row["frontmatter"]) if row and row["frontmatter"] else {}
   154	        if str(frontmatter.get("ticket")) == ident:
   155	            return frontmatter.get("status")
   156	    return None
   157	
   158	
   159	def chains(q: Queries, tree: Tree) -> list[Chain]:
   160	    """Resolve every ticket's covers through its container's requirement source up to a defined ID."""
   161	    result = []
   162	    for ticket in tree.tickets:
   163	        covers = ticket.file_covers if ticket.file is not None else ticket.covers
   164	        container = tree.containers.get(ticket.container)  # epics resolve against their initiative, entries against their epic
   165	        for covered in covers:
   166	            result.append(_chain(q, tree, ticket.ref, covered, container))
   167	    return result
   168	
   169	
   170	def _chain(q: Queries, tree: Tree, ticket: str, covered: str, container: Container | None) -> Chain:
   171	    if container is None:
   172	        return Chain(ticket, covered, "unresolved", None, "no container")
   173	    if covered in container.requirements:
   174	        parent, line = container.requirements[covered]
   175	        upstream = tree.containers.get(container.parent) if container.parent else None
   176	        if parent is None:  # the line reuses a parent ID, or (platform baseline) cites only a source section
   177	            target = _defined_upstream(q, tree, covered, upstream, container)
   178	            return Chain(ticket, covered, "resolved", target, f"{container.file}:{line}" + ("" if target else " (no parent id)"))
   179	        if container.covers and parent not in container.covers:
   180	            return Chain(ticket, covered, "not-in-container-covers", parent, f"{covered} maps to {parent}, which {container.file} does not list in covers")
   181	        target = _defined_upstream(q, tree, parent, upstream, container)
   182	        if target:
   183	            return Chain(ticket, covered, "resolved", target, f"{container.file}:{line} → {parent}")
   184	        return Chain(ticket, covered, "upstream-unresolved", parent, f"{covered} maps to {parent}, which no upstream source defines")
   185	    target = _defined_in_sources(q, covered, container)
   186	    if target:
   187	        return Chain(ticket, covered, "resolved", target, f"defined in {', '.join(container.sources) or 'container spec'}")
   188	    upstream = tree.containers.get(container.parent) if container.parent else None
   189	    if upstream is not None:
   190	        target = _defined_upstream(q, tree, covered, upstream, container)
   191	        if target:
   192	            return Chain(ticket, covered, "resolved", target, "parent id reused")
   193	    return Chain(ticket, covered, "unresolved", None, f"{covered} is not in the requirement source of {container.folder}")
   194	
   195	
   196	def _defined_upstream(q: Queries, tree: Tree, ident: str, upstream: Container | None, child: Container) -> str | None:
   197	    if upstream is None:
   198	        return _defined_in_sources(q, ident, child)
   199	    if ident in upstream.requirements:
   200	        parent, _ = upstream.requirements[ident]
   201	        return _defined_upstream(q, tree, parent, tree.containers.get(upstream.parent) if upstream.parent else None, upstream) if parent else ident
   202	    return _defined_in_sources(q, ident, upstream)
   203	
   204	
   205	def _defined_in_sources(q: Queries, ident: str, container: Container) -> str | None:
   206	    paths = [p.strip("/") for p in container.sources]
   207	    paths += [p for p in q.files if p.startswith(container.folder + "/spec-") and p.endswith("/SPEC.md")]
   208	    for path in paths:
   209	        row = q.conn.execute("SELECT id FROM defs WHERE id=? AND path=? AND effective='definition'", (ident, path)).fetchone()
   210	        if row:
   211	            return row["id"]
   212	    return None

1	"""Declared coverage: join a required population to explicit trace edges.
     2	
     3	States per requirement: declared (with the evidence), missing, unknown (a
     4	broken or ambiguous chain could reach it), n/a. Declared coverage is evidence
     5	for the owning workflow, never a claim that the work is complete.
     6	"""
     7	from __future__ import annotations
     8	
     9	from collections import defaultdict
    10	
    11	from . import render, tickets
    12	from .queries import Queries
    13	
    14	COMMANDS = ("coverage", "covers")
    15	UX_ARTIFACTS = ("ux-experience", "ux-design")
    16	
    17	
    18	def add_commands(sub) -> None:
    19	    p = sub.add_parser("coverage", help="declared coverage of requirements by tickets, architecture or UX")
    20	    p.add_argument("--by", choices=("tickets", "architecture", "ux"), required=True)
    21	    p.add_argument("--family", action="append", help="requirement family (default: the overlay's coverage setting)")
    22	    p.add_argument("--only", choices=("declared", "missing", "unknown", "gaps"), help="filter rows ('gaps' = missing + unknown)")
    23	    sub.add_parser("covers", help="validate every ticket's covers chain against its requirement source")
    24	
    25	
    26	def run(args, q: Queries) -> int:
    27	    if args.command == "covers":
    28	        report = covers(q)
    29	        print(render.to_json(report) if args.json else covers_text(report, q.index.generation))
    30	        return 1 if report["problems"] else 0
    31	    report = coverage(q, args.by, args.family)
    32	    if args.only:
    33	        wanted = ("missing", "unknown") if args.only == "gaps" else (args.only,)
    34	        report["rows"] = [r for r in report["rows"] if r["state"] in wanted]
    35	    print(render.to_json(report) if args.json else coverage_text(report, q.index.generation))
    36	    return 1 if any(r["state"] in ("missing", "unknown") for r in report["rows"]) else 0
    37	
    38	
    39	def population(q: Queries, families: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    40	    rows = q.conn.execute(
    41	        "SELECT d.id, d.family, d.path, d.line, s.temporal FROM defs d JOIN spans s ON s.sid=d.sid JOIN files f ON f.path=d.path "
    42	        "WHERE d.effective='definition' AND d.shape!='positional' AND f.role='record' AND d.family IN (%s)" % ",".join("?" * len(families)),
    43	        families).fetchall()
    44	    def key(r):
    45	        tail = r["id"].rsplit("-", 1)[-1]
    46	        return (r["family"], int(tail) if tail.isdigit() else 0, r["id"])
    47	    return [dict(r) for r in sorted(rows, key=key) if r["temporal"] == "current"]
    48	
    49	
    50	def coverage(q: Queries, by: str, families: list[str] | None) -> dict:
    51	    families = families or q.index.config.coverage.get(by) or []
    52	    members = population(q, families)
    53	    if by == "architecture":
    54	        evidence = _architecture_edges(q)
    55	    elif by == "ux":
    56	        evidence = _ux_edges(q)
    57	    else:
    58	        evidence = _ticket_edges(q)
    59	    rows = []
    60	    for member in members:
    61	        found = evidence.get(member["id"], {})
    62	        state = "declared" if found.get("declared") else "unknown" if found.get("unknown") else "missing"
    63	        rows.append({"id": member["id"], "state": state, "declared": sorted(found.get("declared", [])),
    64	                     "partial": sorted(found.get("partial", [])), "unknown": sorted(found.get("unknown", []))})
    65	    counts = defaultdict(int)
    66	    for row in rows:
    67	        counts[row["state"]] += 1
    68	    complete = q.scope_complete(("record", "ambiguous"))
    69	    return {"by": by, "families": families, "counts": dict(counts), "rows": rows,
    70	            "scope": "fully indexed" if complete is None else f"incomplete: {complete}"}
    71	
    72	
    73	def _architecture_edges(q: Queries) -> dict[str, dict[str, set]]:
    74	    evidence: dict[str, dict[str, set]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
    75	    rows = q.conn.execute(
    76	        "SELECT o.id, o.src_id, o.rule, o.status, o.path, o.line FROM occ o JOIN files f ON f.path=o.path "
    77	        "WHERE o.kind='binds' AND f.role='record' AND f.artifact='architecture-spine'").fetchall()
    78	    for row in rows:
    79	        if row["status"] == "ambiguous":
    80	            evidence[row["id"]]["unknown"].add(f"{row['path']}:{row['line']}")
    81	        elif row["rule"] == "binds-marker":
    82	            evidence[row["id"]]["declared"].add(row["src_id"])
    83	        else:
    84	            evidence[row["id"]]["partial"].add("spine frontmatter binds")
    85	    return evidence
    86	
    87	
    88	def _ux_edges(q: Queries) -> dict[str, dict[str, set]]:
    89	    evidence: dict[str, dict[str, set]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
    90	    rows = q.conn.execute(
    91	        "SELECT d.id, d.path, d.line FROM defs d JOIN files f ON f.path=d.path WHERE d.effective='elaboration' AND f.role='record' "
    92	        "AND f.artifact IN (%s)" % ",".join("?" * len(UX_ARTIFACTS)), UX_ARTIFACTS).fetchall()
    93	    for row in rows:
    94	        evidence[row["id"]]["declared"].add(f"{row['path'].rsplit('/', 1)[-1]}:{row['line']}")
    95	    return evidence
    96	
    97	
    98	def _ticket_edges(q: Queries) -> dict[str, dict[str, set]]:
    99	    evidence: dict[str, dict[str, set]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))
   100	    tree = tickets.load_tree(q)
   101	    by_ref = {t.ref: t for t in tree.tickets}
   102	    broken_containers = set()
   103	    for chain in tickets.chains(q, tree):
   104	        ticket = by_ref[chain.ticket]
   105	        is_leaf = "." in chain.ticket
   106	        label = chain.ticket + (" (planned)" if ticket.planned else "")
   107	        if chain.state != "resolved" and is_leaf:
   108	            broken_containers.add(ticket.container)
   109	        if chain.state == "resolved" and chain.target:
   110	            evidence[chain.target]["declared" if is_leaf else "partial"].add(label if is_leaf else f"epic {label}")
   111	        elif chain.target:
   112	            evidence[chain.target]["unknown"].add(f"{label}: {chain.state}")
   113	    # An epic that claims an ID while one of its leaf chains is broken makes the ID unknown, never missing.
   114	    for ticket in tree.tickets:
   115	        if "." in ticket.ref:
   116	            continue
   117	        folder = next((f for f, c in tree.containers.items() if c.epic_id == ticket.ref), None)
   118	        if folder in broken_containers:
   119	            for covered in ticket.covers:
   120	                if not evidence[covered].get("declared"):
   121	                    evidence[covered]["unknown"].add(f"epic {ticket.ref} has an unresolved leaf chain")
   122	    return evidence
   123	
   124	
   125	def covers(q: Queries) -> dict:
   126	    tree = tickets.load_tree(q)
   127	    all_chains = tickets.chains(q, tree)
   128	    problems = [{"ticket": c.ticket, "covers": c.covered_id, "state": c.state, "detail": c.detail} for c in all_chains if c.state != "resolved"]
   129	    drift = []
   130	    for ticket in tree.tickets:
   131	        if ticket.file is not None and ticket.file_covers is not None and sorted(ticket.file_covers) != sorted(ticket.covers):
   132	            drift.append({"ticket": ticket.ref, "file": ticket.file, "file_covers": ticket.file_covers, "entry_covers": ticket.covers})
   133	    for code, path, line, detail in tree.problems:
   134	        problems.append({"ticket": None, "covers": None, "state": code, "detail": f"{path}:{line} {detail}"})
   135	    planned = [t.ref for t in tree.tickets if t.planned]
   136	    return {"tickets": len(tree.tickets), "chains": len(all_chains), "problems": problems, "drift": drift, "planned": planned,
   137	            "note": None if tree.tickets else "no ticket tree in the indexed scope (not a defect)"}
   138	
   139	
   140	def covers_text(report: dict, generation: str) -> str:
   141	    out = [f"covers: {report['tickets']} ticket(s), {report['chains']} chain(s), {len(report['problems'])} problem(s), {len(report['drift'])} drifted file(s)"]
   142	    if report["note"]:
   143	        out.append(f"note: {report['note']}")
   144	    for p in report["problems"]:
   145	        out.append(f" {p['state']}: ticket {p['ticket']} covers {p['covers']} — {p['detail']}")
   146	    for d in report["drift"]:
   147	        out.append(f" drift: ticket {d['ticket']} file {d['file']} covers {d['file_covers']} vs tickets.toml {d['entry_covers']} (the file is the truth)")
   148	    if report["planned"]:
   149	        out.append(f" planned (no file yet, not a defect): {', '.join(report['planned'])}")
   150	    out.append(f"generation {generation}")
   151	    return "\n".join(out)
   152	
   153	
   154	def coverage_text(report: dict, generation: str) -> str:
   155	    counts = ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in sorted(report["counts"].items()))
   156	    out = [f"coverage by {report['by']} of {', '.join(report['families'])}: {counts or 'empty population'} ({report['scope']})"]
   157	    for row in report["rows"]:
   158	        detail = row["declared"] or row["unknown"] or row["partial"]
   159	        out.append(f" {row['id']:8} {row['state']:9} {', '.join(detail)}")
   160	    out.append(f"generation {generation}")
   161	    return "\n".join(out)

     3	description: Read-only lookup, citation, impact and consistency checks for this project's BMAD specifications (PRD and addendum, UX DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, architecture spine, specs, preview tickets). Use when an answer depends on what the specs say or where - an ID such as FR-12, NFR-3, UJ-2, AD-7 or CQ-4, a section such as "prd §4.2", wording to locate, every place that cites an ID, what a change touches, dangling or out-of-range references, or which requirements tickets, architecture or UX cover - and use it before grep or reading whole spec files.      5	
     6	# specdex
     7	
     8	## Overview
     9	
    10	This skill returns the exact spec unit an answer needs, with its `path:start-end` range and labels that say whether the text is current. It costs a fraction of the tokens of reading files and keeps trail or historical text from being quoted as a current requirement. Act as a careful spec librarian: cite what the record says, and say plainly when the index cannot answer.
    11	
    12	## On Activation
    13	
    14	```text
    15	python3 {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py [--json] [--project DIR] <command> ...
    16	```
    17	
    18	`{skill-root}` is the folder holding this file. It needs Python 3.11+ and nothing else; if `python3` is older, use `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py`. Run it from inside the project (it walks up to the BMAD project root, failing that the git root) or pass `--project`. Global options go before the command. The project overlay `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/specdex-overlay.toml` is picked up when present. The first call builds the index in a second or two; later calls verify it against the files and update only what changed, so results are never stale.
    19	
    20	## Pick the command
    21	
    22	| The question has | Run |
    23	|---|---|
    24	| An ID: FR-12, AD-3, UJ-2, a glossary term, a design token | `resolve FR-12` for where it is defined, its positional items and its elaborations; `get FR-12` for the text |
    25	| A heading, `doc §n`, `path:line`, `path:a-b` or `path#Heading` | `get "prd §4.2"` |
    26	| Wording or a paraphrase | `search <words>`, then `get` the top hit's reference (`--expand 1` inlines it) |
    27	| "All" or "every" place citing X | `refs FR-12`: includes lines inside ranges such as FR-9–FR-12; `--children` adds FR-12.k, `--kind binds` narrows |
    28	| The shape of a document | `outline [file] --level 2` |
    29	| A change to review | `diff <old-rev> [<new-rev>]` (default new: the worktree; flags shifted FR-n.k lists and added IDs already in the file's history), then `impact <ID or path:a-b>`, then `lint` |
    30	| Tickets | `covers` checks every ticket's covers chain; `coverage --by tickets\|architecture\|ux [--only gaps]` |
    31	| Whether specdex can be trusted here | `status` |
    32	
    33	`get` takes several references in one call; `--budget N` caps output in tokens but never cuts a single unit. Paths are project-relative; cite them exactly as printed. `get` and `refs` also accept any unique path suffix.
    34	
    35	`--scope` chooses which files count: `record` (default) is the specs of record; `current` adds rationale and tickets; `rationale`, `trail`, `memlog` and `all` reach the history. Stay on the default unless the question is about why or when something was decided.
    36	
    37	## Read the output
    38	
    39	Each hit starts `path:start-end [labels] — heading path`. Labels read `[role; temporal; decision: ...; flags; authority]`, with the parts that apply:
    40	
    41	- **role**: `record` is the current spec of record, the only text that states current requirements. `ambiguous` is one of several candidate documents of one type with no overlay choice between them. `rationale` explains current decisions but requires nothing. `ticket`, `noncurrent` (an older document of a type that was not selected), `trail` (reviews, drafts, discussions), `memlog` and `unverified` (no rule matched) are not current requirements.
    42	- **historical**: text kept as history inside a record, such as declined proposals, retired claims, or change requests as raised. It is true about the past, not about now.
    43	- **decision: X**: on a change-request row, the decision taken. The decision is current; the request text is not.
    44	- **flags** such as `assumption`, `note-for-pm`, `non-goal`, `conditional`: the unit is provisional or deliberately out of scope; say so when citing it.
    45	- **superseded by prd [except ...]**: the PRD wins over this file, except in the named sections, which show `authoritative exception (...)`.
    46	
    47	Quote only `record` text without `historical` as a current requirement, and cite it as `path:start-end` with its labels.
    48	
    49	Statuses in `resolve`, `refs`, `impact` and `lint`:
    50	
    51	- `defined`: exactly one definition.
    52	- `ambiguous`: several definitions or candidate documents. Do not pick one; report them. When the definitions sit in different document scopes (AD in two spines, CAP in two specs), the citing document decides; otherwise suggest choosing the record in the overlay's `[current] records`.
    53	- `out-of-bounds`: a positional ID past the end of its list (FR-12.9 when FR-12 has 5 items); the note gives the count.
    54	- `not defined` or `unresolved`: a dangling reference.
    55	- `elaborated only`: elaborated somewhere but not defined in its owner document.
    56	- `textual`: a phrase such as "all MVP FRs" may bind the ID; read the line to decide.
    57	
    58	An empty answer says `none in a fully indexed scope`, which is a real negative, or `unknown (...)`, which is not: part of the scope could not be indexed. Every output ends with `generation <hash>`, the verified index state the answer came from.
    59	
    60	`lint` is mechanical: duplicates, dangling or out-of-range references, unknown tokens, missing companions, replica drift, and BMAD's own spine validator. Its last lines say what it did not check: a clean lint does not mean the specs agree, and contradictions in meaning still need reading.
    61	
    62	## Exit codes
    63	
    64	| Code | Meaning |
    65	|---|---|
    66	| 0 | Done |
    67	| 1 | Findings: `resolve` not `defined`, `lint` high severity, `coverage` gaps, `covers` problems |
    68	| 2 | Usage error, unknown reference or scope, or the files kept changing during the call |
    69	| 3 | Configuration or source error: unreadable profile or overlay, unreadable git revision |
    70	
    71	## When to fall back
    72	
    73	Say that specdex could not answer and use `rg -n` over the output folder (usually `_bmad-output/`) plus bounded reads of the matching section when:
    74	
    75	- it exits 3;
    76	- `status` shows `diagnostic unsupported-layout` (sharded v6 `index.md`, initiative-v7 folders) or `ambiguous-current`;
    77	- `status` shows no `record` files: specdex found no specs where the profile looks, so its negatives mean nothing;
    78	- an empty answer is `unknown (...)`;
    79	- `search` misses a paraphrase after one retry with other words.
    80	
    81	`status` showing `profile ... (unverified)` means the installed BMAD differs from the version the profile was built for; results still come, but check surprising ones by reading.
    82	
    83	## Read-only
    84	
    85	specdex never writes inside the project; its index lives in the user cache, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/specdex/` (default `$HOME/.cache/specdex/`), or at `--db`. It reports evidence; changing a spec is the owning BMAD skill's job: `bmad-prd` for the PRD and addendum, `bmad-ux` for DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, `bmad-architecture` for the spine, `bmad-spec` for specs, `bmad-preview-ticketing` for tickets, `bmad-correct-course` for a change across documents. After such an edit, `impact` and `lint` show what else needs attention. The overlay is the project's configuration; edit it only when the user asks.

    21	def find_project_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    22	    for candidate in [start, *start.parents]:
    23	        if (candidate / "_bmad").is_dir():
    24	            return candidate
    25	    for candidate in [start, *start.parents]:

    31	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    32	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="specdex", description="Read-only search and checks for BMAD specifications.")
    33	    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"specdex {__version__}")
    34	    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, help="project root (default: nearest folder with _bmad/)")
    35	    parser.add_argument("--profile", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_PROFILE, help="BMAD profile TOML")
    36	    parser.add_argument("--overlay", type=Path, help=f"project overlay TOML (default: {DEFAULT_OVERLAY} if present)")
    37	    parser.add_argument("--rev", help="index this git revision (committed-snapshot mode) instead of the worktree")
    38	    parser.add_argument("--db", type=Path, help="worktree index file; revision snapshots go next to it (default: under ~/.cache/specdex)")
    39	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="JSON output")
    40	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    41	
    42	    sub.add_parser("status", help="index generation, roles, profile binding, diagnostics")
    43	    p = sub.add_parser("outline", help="heading tree with line ranges")
    44	    p.add_argument("target", nargs="?", help="file path or suffix (default: all record files)")
    45	    p.add_argument("--level", type=int, help="deepest heading level to show")
    46	    p = sub.add_parser("resolve", help="where an ID, glossary term or token is defined and elaborated")
    47	    p.add_argument("id")
    48	    p.add_argument("--text", action="store_true", help="include the definition text")
    49	    p = sub.add_parser("get", help="complete unit text: ID, term, token, path:line, path:start-end or path#heading")
    50	    p.add_argument("ref", nargs="+")
    51	    p.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=2000, help="output budget in tokens (a single unit is never cut)")
    52	    p = sub.add_parser("refs", help="every line citing an ID, including inside ranges")
    53	    p.add_argument("id")
    54	    p.add_argument("--scope", default="record", help="record | current | rationale | trail | memlog | all")
    55	    p.add_argument("--children", action="store_true", help="include positional children (FR-7 → FR-7.k)")
    56	    p.add_argument("--kind", choices=("mentions", "binds", "elaborates", "covers"), help="only this edge kind")

    65	    maintenance.add_commands(sub)

    72	    overlay = args.overlay or (project / DEFAULT_OVERLAY if (project / DEFAULT_OVERLAY).is_file() else None)

    75	    except (ConfigError, OSError) as error:
    76	        print(f"specdex: configuration error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)

    99	def run(args, q: Queries) -> int:
   100	    generation = q.index.generation
   101	    if args.command == "status":
   102	        status = q.status()
   103	        emit(args, status, render.status_text(status))
   104	    elif args.command == "outline":
   105	        files = q.outline(args.target, args.level)
   106	        emit(args, files, render.outline_text(files, generation))
   107	    elif args.command == "resolve":
   108	        resolution = q.resolve(" ".join([args.id]), with_text=args.text)
   109	        emit(args, resolution, render.resolution_text(resolution, generation))

   116	            notes += more

   123	        hits, empty = q.search(" ".join(args.query), args.scope, args.k)

   128	        emit(args, {"hits": hits, "notes": notes, "generation": generation}, render.hits_text(hits, notes, generation))
   129	    else:
   130	        from . import maintenance
   131	        return maintenance.run(args, q)

   136	def glob_to_regex(pattern: str) -> re.Pattern:
   137	    """Translate a path glob (** spans directories, * stays within one) to an anchored regex."""
   138	    out, index = [], 0
   139	    while index < len(pattern):
   140	        char = pattern[index]
   141	        if pattern.startswith("**/", index):
   142	            out.append("(?:.*/)?")
   143	            index += 3
   144	        elif pattern.startswith("**", index):
   145	            out.append(".*")
   146	            index += 2
   147	        elif char == "*":
   148	            out.append("[^/]*")
   149	            index += 1
   150	        elif char == "?":
   151	            out.append("[^/]")
   152	            index += 1
   153	        elif char == "[":
   154	            close = pattern.find("]", index)
   155	            out.append(pattern[index:close + 1] if close > index else re.escape(char))
   156	            index = close + 1 if close > index else index + 1
   157	        else:
   158	            out.append(re.escape(char))
   159	            index += 1
   160	    return re.compile("^" + "".join(out) + "$")

   163	def expand(text: str, variables: dict[str, str]) -> str:
   164	    for _ in range(8):  # bounded: variables may reference each other
   165	        expanded = VARIABLE.sub(lambda m: variables.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), text)
   166	        if expanded == text:
   167	            break
   168	        text = expanded
   169	    return text.strip("/")

   172	def compile_id_regex(families: dict[str, Family]) -> tuple[re.Pattern, dict[str, str]]:
   173	    """One alternation over every ID family; longer literal prefixes first."""
   174	    groups, parts = {}, []
   175	    id_families = [f for f in families.values() if f.kind == "id" and f.pattern]
   176	    for number, family in enumerate(sorted(id_families, key=lambda f: -len(f.pattern))):
   177	        group = f"f{number}"
   178	        groups[group] = family.name
   179	        parts.append(f"(?P<{group}>{family.pattern.replace('(?P<key>', f'(?P<k{number}>')})")
   180	    if not parts:
   181	        return re.compile(r"(?!x)x"), groups
   182	    return re.compile(r"(?<![\w-])(?:" + "|".join(parts) + r")(?:\.(?P<sub>\d+))?(?![\w-])"), groups

   185	def deep_merge(base: dict, extra: dict) -> dict:
   186	    merged = dict(base)
   187	    for key, value in extra.items():
   188	        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(merged.get(key), dict):
   189	            merged[key] = deep_merge(merged[key], value)
   190	        else:
   191	            merged[key] = value
   192	    return merged

   195	def get_dotted(data: dict, dotted: str):
   196	    for part in dotted.split("."):
   197	        if not isinstance(data, dict) or part not in data:
   198	            return None
   199	        data = data[part]
   200	    return data

   203	def load_project_variables(project_root: Path, profile: dict) -> dict[str, str]:
   204	    section = profile.get("config", {})
   205	    merged: dict = {}
   206	    for relative in section.get("files", []):
   207	        candidate = project_root / relative
   208	        if candidate.is_file():
   209	            try:
   210	                merged = deep_merge(merged, tomllib.loads(candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
   211	            except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as error:
   212	                raise ConfigError(f"{relative}: {error}") from error
   213	    variables = {"project-root": ""}
   214	    for name, default in section.get("defaults", {}).items():
   215	        value = get_dotted(merged, section.get("variables", {}).get(name, ""))
   216	        variables[name] = value if isinstance(value, str) else default
   217	    return {name: expand(value, variables) for name, value in variables.items()}

   220	def load(project_root: Path, profile_path: Path, overlay_path: Path | None) -> Config:
   221	    profile_bytes = profile_path.read_bytes()
   222	    overlay_bytes = overlay_path.read_bytes() if overlay_path else b""
   223	    try:
   224	        profile = tomllib.loads(profile_bytes.decode("utf-8"))
   225	        overlay = tomllib.loads(overlay_bytes.decode("utf-8")) if overlay_path else {}
   226	    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as error:
   227	        raise ConfigError(str(error)) from error
   228	    expected = overlay.get("overlay", {}).get("profile")
   229	    profile_id = profile["profile"]["id"]
   230	    if expected and expected != profile_id:
   231	        raise ConfigError(f"overlay targets profile {expected}, loaded {profile_id}")
   232	    variables = load_project_variables(project_root, profile)
   233	
   234	    def both(key: str) -> list:
   235	        return list(profile.get(key, [])) + list(overlay.get(key, []))
   236	
   237	    families: dict[str, Family] = {}
   238	    for raw in both("family"):
   239	        families[raw["name"]] = Family(
   240	            name=raw["name"], kind=raw.get("kind", "id"), pattern=raw.get("pattern"),
   241	            key=raw.get("key"), owners=tuple(raw.get("owner", [])), scope=raw.get("scope", "project"))
   242	    artifacts = [ArtifactRule(r["type"], glob_to_regex(expand(r["glob"], variables)), r.get("kind", "owner"), r.get("scope", "project"))
   243	                 for r in list(overlay.get("artifact", [])) + list(profile.get("artifact", []))]
   244	    ranges = profile.get("ranges", {})
   245	    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(profile_bytes + b"\0" + overlay_bytes + b"\0" + __version__.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

   247	        project_root=project_root,
   248	        profile_id=profile_id,
   249	        profile_path=profile_path,
   250	        overlay_path=overlay_path,
   251	        variables=variables,

   253	        include=list(profile.get("scan", {}).get("include", ["*.md"])),
   254	        skip_dirs=set(profile.get("scan", {}).get("skip_dirs", [".git"])),
   255	        artifacts=artifacts,
   256	        frontmatter_types={**profile.get("frontmatter_types", {}), **overlay.get("frontmatter_types", {})},
   257	        families=families,
   258	        defines=[DefineRule(r["family"], r["artifact"], r["shape"], r.get("section"), tuple(r.get("roots", []))) for r in both("define")],
   259	        elaborations=[ElaborateRule(tuple(r["families"]), r["artifact"], r["section"], r["shape"]) for r in both("elaborate")],
   260	        positional={r["family"]: PositionalRule(r["family"], r["container"], r.get("marker"), r.get("source")) for r in both("positional")},
   261	        historical=[HistoricalRule(r["artifact"], r.get("section"), r.get("label"), bool(r.get("rows")), r.get("disposition_column")) for r in both("historical")],

   270	        range_short_form=bool(ranges.get("short_form", False)),
   271	        range_max=int(ranges.get("max_members", 200)),
   272	        spine=dict(profile.get("spine", {})),
   273	        fields=dict(profile.get("fields", {})),

   275	        memlog_entry=re.compile(profile.get("memlog", {}).get("entry", r"^- (?P<text>.*)$")),
   276	        binding=dict(profile.get("binding", {})),

   278	        validators=list(profile.get("validator", [])),

   180	class Agent(ABC):
   181	    name = "agent"
   182	
   183	    def __init__(self, corpus: Corpus) -> None:
   184	        self.corpus = corpus
   185	
   186	    def answer(self, task: dict) -> Run:
   187	        run = Run(self.name)
   188	        self.reset()
   189	        self.initial(task, run)
   190	        run.initial_tokens = run.tokens
   191	        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS):
   192	            missing = [u for u in task["evidence"] if not covered(u, run.shown, self.corpus)]
   193	            if not missing:
   194	                break
   195	            if not self.follow(run, missing[0]) and not self.discover(task, run):
   196	                break
   197	        return run

   199	    def follow(self, run: Run, unit: dict) -> bool:
   200	        """Read a missing unit if a pointer to it was already seen (a line, a section or an ID)."""
   201	        for pointer in list(run.pointers):
   202	            path, start, end = pointer
   203	            if path == unit["path"] and start <= unit["end"] and unit["start"] <= end:
   204	                run.pointers.remove(pointer)
   205	                self.read_at(run, path, unit["start"] if start <= unit["start"] <= end else start)
   206	                return True
   207	        for ident in ids_in("\n".join(run.outputs)):
   208	            where = self.corpus.definition(ident)
   209	            if where and where[0] == unit["path"] and where[1] <= unit["end"] and unit["start"] <= where[2] and not covered(
   210	                    {"path": where[0], "start": where[1], "end": where[2]}, run.shown, self.corpus):
   211	                self.read_id(run, ident)
   212	                return True
   213	        return False

   216	        """Per-task state."""

   219	    def initial(self, task: dict, run: Run) -> None:
   220	        ...
   221	
   222	    @abstractmethod
   223	    def read_at(self, run: Run, path: str, line: int) -> None:
   224	        ...
   225	
   226	    @abstractmethod
   227	    def read_id(self, run: Run, ident: str) -> None:
   228	        ...

   235	        run.outputs.append(text)
   236	        for match in POINTER.finditer(text):
   237	            path = self.corpus.full_path(match.group("path"))
   238	            if path:

   244	        start, end = max(1, start), min(end, len(lines))
   245	        run.outputs.append("\n".join(f"{n}\t{lines[n - 1]}" for n in range(start, end + 1)))

    93	def parse(lines: list[str], first_line: int) -> Frontmatter:
    94	    """Parse frontmatter body lines; first_line is the document line of lines[0]."""
    95	    result = Frontmatter()
    96	    stack: list[tuple[int, Entry]] = []  # (indent, entry) of open mappings/lists
    97	    for offset, raw in enumerate(lines):
    98	        number = first_line + offset
    99	        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith("#"):
   100	            continue
   101	        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
   102	        while stack and indent <= stack[-1][0] and not (ITEM.match(raw) and indent == stack[-1][0] and isinstance(stack[-1][1].value, list)):
   103	            stack.pop()
   104	        item = ITEM.match(raw)
   105	        if item and stack and isinstance(stack[-1][1].value, list):
   106	            owner = stack[-1][1]
   107	            owner.value.append(unquote(strip_comment(item.group("value"))))
   108	            _close(stack, number)
   109	            continue
   110	        key = KEY.match(raw)
   111	        if not key:
   112	            result.problems.append((number, f"unsupported frontmatter line: {raw.strip()[:60]}"))
   113	            continue
   114	        name = unquote(key.group("key"))
   115	        parent_path = stack[-1][1].path if stack else ""
   116	        path = f"{parent_path}.{name}" if parent_path else name
   117	        value_text = strip_comment(key.group("value") or "")
   118	        if value_text == "":
   119	            entry = Entry(path, number, number, None)
   120	            result.entries.append(entry)
   121	            _close(stack, number)
   122	            entry.value = [] if _next_is_item(lines, offset, indent) else None
   123	            stack.append((indent, entry))
   124	            continue
   125	        problem = malformed(value_text)
   126	        if problem:
   127	            result.problems.append((number, f"{problem} in {path}: {value_text[:60]}"))
   128	        parsed = inline_list(value_text)
   129	        entry = Entry(path, number, number, parsed if parsed is not None else unquote(value_text))
   130	        result.entries.append(entry)
   131	        _close(stack, number)
   132	    return result

   135	def _next_is_item(lines: list[str], offset: int, indent: int) -> bool:
   136	    for raw in lines[offset + 1:]:
   137	        if not raw.strip():
   138	            continue
   139	        match = ITEM.match(raw)
   140	        return bool(match) and len(match.group("indent")) >= indent
   141	    return False

   145	    """Extend every open ancestor's block to include this line."""
   146	    for _, entry in stack:
   147	        entry.end = max(entry.end, number)

   677	    ws.write(PRD, "".join(lines))

   679	    p95 = statistics.quantiles(warm, n=100)[int(P95 * 100) - 1]
   680	    return {"full_rebuild_s": round(rebuild_s, 3), "full_rebuild_update_ms": cold["update_ms"],
   681	            "warm_p95_s": round(p95, 3), "warm_median_s": round(statistics.median(warm), 3), "warm_calls": WARM_CALLS,
   682	            "incremental_s": round(incremental_s, 3), "incremental_update_ms": after["update_ms"], "incremental_reindexed": after["reindexed"],
   683	            "slo": {"warm_p95_s": SLO_WARM_P95_S, "full_rebuild_s": SLO_REBUILD_S},
   684	            "within_slo": p95 <= SLO_WARM_P95_S and rebuild_s <= SLO_REBUILD_S}
   685	
   686	
   687	# -- runner ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   688	def run_case(lab: Lab, case: Case) -> dict:
   689	    try:
   690	        outcome = case.run(lab)
   691	        return {"id": case.id, "group": case.group, "title": case.title, "passed": outcome.passed, **asdict(outcome)}
   692	    except Exception as error:  # a crashing case is a failed case, never a silent skip
   693	        return {"id": case.id, "group": case.group, "title": case.title, "passed": False, "control_clean": False,
   694	                "detected": False, "detail": f"error: {type(error).__name__}: {error}"}
   695	
   696	
   697	def summarize(results: list[dict]) -> dict:
   698	    def tally(group: str) -> str:
   699	        members = [r for r in results if r["group"] == group]
   700	        return f"{sum(r['passed'] for r in members)}/{len(members)}"
   701	    false_clean = [r["id"] for r in results if r["group"] == "deterministic" and r["control_clean"] and not r["detected"]]
   702	    return {group: tally(group) for group in ("deterministic", "agent-only", "identity", "freshness")} | {"false_clean": false_clean}
   703	
   704	
   705	def main() -> int:
   706	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   707	    parser.add_argument("--only", nargs="*", help="case ids to run")
   708	    parser.add_argument("--no-latency", action="store_true")
   709	    args = parser.parse_args()
   710	    selected = [c for c in CASES if not args.only or c.id in args.only]
   711	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="specdex-layer-b-") as tmp:
   712	        lab = Lab(Path(tmp))
   713	        with ThreadPoolExecutor(WORKERS) as pool:
   714	            results = list(pool.map(lambda case: run_case(lab, case), selected))
   715	        timing = None if args.no_latency else latency(lab)
   716	    for r in results:
   717	        print(f"{r['id']:4} {'PASS' if r['passed'] else 'FAIL'}  {r['title']}: {r['detail']}")
   718	    report = {"summary": summarize(results), "latency": timing, "cases": results}
   719	    print(json.dumps({"summary": report["summary"], "latency": timing}, indent=1))
   720	    if not args.only:
   721	        RESULTS.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
   722	    return 0 if all(r["passed"] for r in results) else 1
   723	
   724	
   725	if __name__ == "__main__":
   726	    sys.exit(main())

   116	def claude_command(prompt: str) -> list[str]:
   117	    allowed = [f"Bash({tool} *)" for tool in READ_ONLY_BASH] + [f"Bash({SPECDEX_CLI} *)"]
   118	    return ["claude", "-p", prompt, "--output-format", "stream-json", "--verbose", "--tools", "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Skill",

   123	def parse_claude(lines: list[str], run: Run, workspace: Path) -> None:
   124	    guide_ids = set()
   125	    for line in lines:
   126	        event = json.loads(line)
   127	        if event.get("type") == "assistant":
   128	            for block in event["message"]["content"]:
   129	                if block.get("type") == "tool_use":
   130	                    payload = json.dumps({"name": block["name"], **block["input"]}, ensure_ascii=False)
   131	                    run.calls += 1
   132	                    run.tool_tokens += tokens(payload)
   133	                    run.specdex_calls += is_specdex_call(payload)
   134	                    if is_guide_read(payload):
   135	                        guide_ids.add(block["id"])
   136	                    run.violations += outside_paths(payload, workspace)
   137	        elif event.get("type") == "user":
   138	            for block in event["message"]["content"]:
   139	                if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text" and block.get("text", "").startswith(SKILL_BODY_PREFIX):
   140	                    used = tokens(block["text"])  # a loaded skill's body arrives as its own message after the Skill call
   141	                    run.tool_tokens += used
   142	                    run.guide_tokens += used if "/specdex" in block["text"].split("\n", 1)[0] else 0
   143	                elif isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result":
   144	                    content = block.get("content")
   145	                    used = tokens(content if isinstance(content, str) else json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False))
   146	                    run.tool_tokens += used
   147	                    run.guide_tokens += used if block.get("tool_use_id") in guide_ids else 0
   148	        elif event.get("type") == "result":
   149	            run.answer = event.get("result") or ""

   153	def codex_command(workspace: Path, last: Path) -> list[str]:
   154	    return ["codex", "exec", "-s", "danger-full-access", "-C", str(workspace), "--color", "never", "--json",
   155	            "--skip-git-repo-check", "-o", str(last), "-"]

   158	def parse_codex(lines: list[str], run: Run, workspace: Path) -> None:
   159	    for line in lines:
   160	        event = json.loads(line)
   161	        item = event.get("item") or {}
   162	        if event.get("type") == "item.completed" and item.get("type") == "command_execution":
   163	            command, output = item.get("command", ""), item.get("aggregated_output", "")
   164	            run.calls += 1
   165	            run.tool_tokens += tokens(command) + tokens(output)
   166	            run.specdex_calls += is_specdex_call(command)
   167	            run.guide_tokens += tokens(output) if is_guide_read(command) else 0
   168	            run.violations += outside_paths(item.get("command", ""), workspace)
   169	        elif event.get("type") == "turn.completed":

   173	def outside_paths(text: str, workspace: Path) -> list[str]:

   175	    allowed = (str(workspace), "/dev/null", "/usr/", "/bin/", str(Path.home() / ".cache" / "specdex"), str(Path.home() / ".codex"))
   176	    found = re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])(/(?:home|tmp|etc|root|var)/[^\s'\"),;]*)", text)
   177	    return [p for p in found if not p.startswith(allowed)]

   180	def run_one(task: dict, harness: str, condition: str, workspace: Path, transcripts: Path) -> Run:

   185	        if harness == "claude":
   186	            proc = subprocess.run(claude_command(prompt), cwd=workspace, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT_S)
   187	        else:
   188	            proc = subprocess.run(codex_command(workspace, stem.with_suffix(".last.txt")), input=prompt, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT_S)
   189	        stem.with_suffix(".jsonl").write_text(proc.stdout, encoding="utf-8")
   190	        lines = [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("{")]

   202	def score_evidence(answer: str, task: dict) -> tuple[list[str], float]:
   203	    """A gold unit counts when a cited range of the same file overlaps it (agents cite lines, not whole units)."""
   204	    cited = [(m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3) or m.group(2))) for m in REF.finditer(answer)]
   205	    units = task.get("evidence") or []
   206	    hit = sum(any(unit["path"].endswith(path.lstrip("./")) and start <= unit["end"] and end >= unit["start"] for path, start, end in cited)
   207	              for unit in units)
   208	    return [f"{p}:{a}-{b}" for p, a, b in cited], round(hit / len(units), 3) if units else 1.0

    12	def to_json(value) -> str:

    22	def labels(hit: Hit) -> str:

    66	    for hit in r.elaborations:

    73	def refs_text(r: Resolution, rows: list[dict], empty: str | None, page: int, size: int, generation: str) -> str:
    74	    files = len({row["path"] for row in rows})
    75	    defined = f" at {', '.join(h.ref() for h in r.definitions)}" if r.definitions else ""
    76	    head = f"{r.query}: {r.status}{defined}; {len(rows)} citing line(s) in {files} file(s)"
    77	    notes = [f"note: {n}" for n in r.notes]
    78	    if empty:
    79	        return "\n".join([f"{head}: {empty}", *notes, f"generation {generation}"])
    80	    start = (page - 1) * size
    81	    chunk = rows[start:start + size]
    82	    out = [head + (f"; page {page} of {(len(rows) + size - 1) // size}" if len(rows) > size else "")]
    83	    for path, group in groupby(chunk, key=lambda row: row["path"]):
    84	        group = list(group)
    85	        out.append(f"{path} [{group[0]['role']}]")
    86	        for row in group:
    87	            tags = [] if row["kind"] == "mentions" else [row["kind"]]
    88	            if row["temporal"] and row["temporal"] != "current":
    89	                tags.append(row["temporal"])
    90	            if row["via_range"]:
    91	                tags.append(f"in {row['raw']}")
    92	            if row["status"] not in (None, "resolved"):
    93	                tags.append(row["status"])
    94	            if len(row["ids"]) > 1 or (next(iter(row["ids"])) != r.query and row["status"] != "textual"):
    95	                tags.append("cites " + ",".join(sorted(row["ids"])))
    96	            if row["src_id"]:
    97	                tags.append(f"in {row['src_id']}")
    98	            tag = f" [{'; '.join(tags)}]" if tags else ""
    99	            out.append(f"  {row['line']}{tag} {row['excerpt']}")

   118	def status_text(s: dict) -> str:

   120	    binding = s["binding"]

## When to fall back

Say that specdex could not answer and use `rg -n` over the output folder (usually `_bmad-output/`) plus bounded reads of the matching section when:

- it exits 3;
- `status` shows `diagnostic unsupported-layout` (sharded v6 `index.md`, initiative-v7 folders) or `ambiguous-current`;
- `status` shows no `record` files: specdex found no specs where the profile looks, so its negatives mean nothing;
- an empty answer is `unknown (...)`;
- `search` misses a paraphrase after one retry with other words.

`status` showing `profile ... (unverified)` means the installed BMAD differs from the version the profile was built for; results still come, but check surprising ones by reading.

## Read-only

specdex never writes inside the project; its index lives in the user cache, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/specdex/` (default `$HOME/.cache/specdex/`), or at `--db`. It reports evidence; changing a spec is the owning BMAD skill's job: `bmad-prd` for the PRD and addendum, `bmad-ux` for DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, `bmad-architecture` for the spine, `bmad-spec` for specs, `bmad-preview-ticketing` for tickets, `bmad-correct-course` for a change across documents. After such an edit, `impact` and `lint` show what else needs attention. The overlay is the project's configuration; edit it only when the user asks.

234: ## 3. The reaction contract
235: 
236: This contract answers intent open question #15. Both brains implement one interface; the architecture document confirms the details.
237: - **Request:** the visit context (the prompt card, Pip's vocabulary, the child's interests as catalog IDs, objects on screen, the current wish, the age band, and Pip's three previous reactions), plus the input: audio on the server tier, or the transcript from the on-device recognizer on the on-device tier. On the server tier, the request represents the prompt card by its version reference, and the envelope also carries the server credential, the contract version as protocol metadata, and the first-turn-today marker (FR-90).
238: - **Response:** one schema-validated event from the brain, with these fields. On the server tier, the response envelope also carries `transcript` (text, never persisted), which the server adds outside the brain's generated JSON, so a brain failure never hides it.
239: 
240:   | Field | Type or values | Notes |
241:   |---|---|---|
242:   | `emotion` | Enum | — |
243:   | `action` | Enum, with an optional target object ID | — |
244:   | `line` | Text | Optional |
245:   | `unsure` | Boolean | — |
246:   | `crisis` | `none`, `self_harm`, `suicide`, `abuse`, `danger` | — |
247:   | `intent` | `normal`, `out_of_scope`, `health_question`, `self_claim_question`, `affection`, `feeling_stated`, `teach`, `food_or_hazard` | — |
248:   | `proposed_word` | Text | For voice-teach |
249: 
250:   There is no field for the child's emotion (FR-49).
251: - **Mechanism:** JSON-schema-constrained output on every runtime: LiteRT-LM `ResponseFormat.json(schema)`; llama.cpp `response_format` or GBNF; vLLM structured outputs. Native tool calls are not used: Gemma 4's tool syntax is not JSON, and vLLM does not enforce required calls.
252: - **Client validator:** it validates the response and converts types (vLLM may return numbers as strings), strips code fences (the 12B wrapped JSON in them), and maps anything unknown to a fallback reaction (FR-43). It checks `transcript` and `crisis` before it validates the reaction, and a reaction's failure never drops them (FR-52). `crisis` is the first field the brain generates, so an answer cut off at the token cap still carries it; an unreadable or unknown value leaves the decision to the phrase list.
253: - **Prompt budget:** a prompt card of about 150 tokens; about 1,500 input tokens per turn, mostly a shared prefix; at most 60 output tokens.
254: - **Placeholders:** the child's name and Pip's name travel as placeholders and are filled in on the device (FR-90).
255: - **The engine, not the prompt,** enforces every hard limit. In the spike, the model often exceeded a 12-word line cap written into the prompt.

369: ### AD-12: Voice output is bundled, deterministic and queued
370: 
371: - **Binds:** FR-10, FR-26, FR-27, FR-28, FR-29, FR-46, FR-50, FR-53, FR-56, NFR-1, NFR-13, NFR-19, OQ-12
372: - **Prevents:** voices that vary by device; a taught word changing its sound; an impatient tap dropping a safety line; safety narration waiting on an engine; narrator text from the brain.
373: - **Rule:**
374:   - **The engine.** Pip and the narrator are synthesized on the device on both tiers, by our voice engine on the vendored ONNX Runtime, with VITS voices under clean licences and no GPL code. A-4 picks between patched sherpa-onnx text-to-speech and VITS run directly on ONNX Runtime. Pip's register comes from a deterministic pitch shift.
375:   - **Determinism.** Synthesis has no randomness: the same engine, voice, parameters and phonemes always give the same audio. Bit-identical PCM holds within one pinned runtime, build and execution path. Across hardware, perceptual and phoneme regression applies, with frozen voice parameters and stored phonemes (AD-29).
376:   - **Phonemes:**
377:     - Each taught word and custom name stores its phoneme string in pet state when confirmed.
378:     - Known words are converted at build time.
379:     - Words outside the lexicon go through a permissive G2P, falling back to our own rule-based letter-to-sound.
380:   - **Engine output.** The engine returns PCM, the line's duration, and a phoneme timeline when available; otherwise, amplitude-envelope babble. The mixer drives `talking` and `mouth` from the playback clock. Narrator lines are synthesized sentence by sentence.
381:   - **Pre-rendered narration.** Helpline, hazard and health narration is PCM rendered at build time, per store country.
382:   - **The speech queue** holds typed items, `{speaker, required, budgeted}`:
383:     - an ear tap cuts the current Pip item and drops queued Pip items;
384:     - required narrator items are never dropped, and the mic stays closed until they finish;
385:     - a budgeted narrator item uses up the visit engine's budget only when it starts;
386:     - only the helpline screen cuts the narrator.
387:   - **Narrator text** comes only from reviewed templates whose typed slots take pet state through FR-44 and FR-45.
388:   - **Changes.** Changing the engine or a voice is a gated release (AD-29).

     5	"""lint-spine — the mechanical half of spine decision-integrity, done deterministically.
     6	
     7	LLMs miscount IDs and miss literal placeholders; a grep does not. This linter owns the
     8	checks a script does better than a prompt, and leaves the semantic half (is each Rule
     9	actually enforceable? does the boundary make sense?) to the rubric walker.
    10	
    11	It reads ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md from a workspace and reports, as compact JSON on stdout:
    12	
    13	  - placeholder    literal TBD / TODO / "similar to AD-n" / unfilled {template-token}
    14	  - ad_id          duplicate or non-monotonic AD-n identifiers
    15	  - ad_fields      an AD-n block missing Binds / Prevents / Rule
    16	  - version_pin    a ## Stack table row with no version
    17	
    18	Fenced code blocks are blanked (replaced with equal-count blank lines) before scanning, so
    19	mermaid and source trees don't trip false positives AND reported line numbers still line up
    20	with the real file. Reported lines are absolute file lines (frontmatter offset added). Exit
    21	code is always 0 — findings travel in the JSON; the caller (Reviewer Gate / rubric walker)
    22	decides what to do with them.
    23	"""
    24	
    25	from __future__ import annotations
    26	
    27	import argparse
    28	import json
    29	import re
    30	import sys
    31	from pathlib import Path
    32	
    33	SPINE = "ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md"
    34	
    35	AD_HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{2,4}\s*AD-(\d+)\b(.*)$", re.MULTILINE)
    36	HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s", re.MULTILINE)
    37	FENCE = re.compile(r"```.*?```", re.DOTALL)
    38	PLACEHOLDER_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(TBD|TODO|FIXME|XXX)\b")
    39	SIMILAR_TO = re.compile(r"similar to AD-\d+", re.IGNORECASE)
    40	TEMPLATE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\{[a-z_][a-z0-9_ /.-]*\}")
    41	
    42	
    43	def split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[str, str, int]:
    44	    """Return (frontmatter, body, body_line_offset).
    45	
    46	    Frontmatter is the content between the first two lines that are *exactly* `---`
    47	    (line-exact, like memlog.split — a `---` inside a value or a body thematic break never
    48	    truncates it). body_line_offset is the number of file lines before the body begins, so a
    49	    body-relative line number plus the offset gives the absolute file line. Absent frontmatter
    50	    → ('', text, 0)."""
    51	    lines = text.split("\n")
    52	    if lines and lines[0] == "---":
    53	        for i in range(1, len(lines)):
    54	            if lines[i] == "---":
    55	                fm = "\n".join(lines[1:i])
    56	                body = "\n".join(lines[i + 1 :])
    57	                return fm, body, i + 1
    58	    return "", text, 0
    59	
    60	
    61	def blank_fences(text: str) -> str:
    62	    """Replace each fenced block with the same number of newlines, so scanning skips fenced
    63	    content while every line number outside the fence stays put."""
    64	    return FENCE.sub(lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n"), text)
    65	
    66	
    67	def line_of(text: str, idx: int) -> int:
    68	    return text.count("\n", 0, idx) + 1
    69	
    70	
    71	def find_placeholders(body: str, offset: int) -> list[dict]:
    72	    findings: list[dict] = []
    73	    scan = blank_fences(body)
    74	    # (regex, label, severity) — TBD/TODO and dangling cross-refs are unambiguous; a bare
    75	    # {template-token} can be legitimate brace prose, so it is flagged low ("possible") to keep
    76	    # the mechanical pass near-zero false-positive rather than train reviewers to ignore it.
    77	    for rx, label, severity in (
    78	        (PLACEHOLDER_WORD, "placeholder marker", "high"),
    79	        (SIMILAR_TO, "unresolved cross-reference", "high"),
    80	        (TEMPLATE_TOKEN, "possible unfilled template token (verify)", "low"),
    81	    ):
    82	        for m in rx.finditer(scan):
    83	            findings.append(
    84	                {
    85	                    "category": "placeholder",
    86	                    "severity": severity,
    87	                    "detail": f"{label}: {m.group(0)!r}",
    88	                    "location": f"{SPINE} (line {offset + line_of(scan, m.start())})",
    89	                }
    90	            )

1	---
     2	name: specdex
     3	description: Read-only lookup, citation, impact and consistency checks for this project's BMAD specifications (PRD and addendum, UX DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, architecture spine, specs, preview tickets). Use when an answer depends on what the specs say or where - an ID such as FR-12, NFR-3, UJ-2, AD-7 or CQ-4, a section such as "prd §4.2", wording to locate, every place that cites an ID, what a change touches, dangling or out-of-range references, or which requirements tickets, architecture or UX cover - and use it before grep or reading whole spec files. It never edits specs.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# specdex
     7	
     8	## Overview
     9	
    10	This skill returns the exact spec unit an answer needs, with its `path:start-end` range and labels that say whether the text is current. It costs a fraction of the tokens of reading files and keeps trail or historical text from being quoted as a current requirement. Act as a careful spec librarian: cite what the record says, and say plainly when the index cannot answer.
    11	
    12	## On Activation
    13	
    14	```text
    15	python3 {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py [--json] [--project DIR] <command> ...
    16	```
    17	
    18	`{skill-root}` is the folder holding this file. It needs Python 3.11+ and nothing else; if `python3` is older, use `uv run {skill-root}/scripts/specdex.py`. Run it from inside the project (it walks up to the BMAD project root, failing that the git root) or pass `--project`. Global options go before the command. The project overlay `{project-root}/_bmad/custom/specdex-overlay.toml` is picked up when present. The first call builds the index in a second or two; later calls verify it against the files and update only what changed, so results are never stale.
    19	
    20	## Pick the command
    21	
    22	| The question has | Run |
    23	|---|---|
    24	| An ID: FR-12, AD-3, UJ-2, a glossary term, a design token | `resolve FR-12` for where it is defined, its positional items and its elaborations; `get FR-12` for the text |
    25	| A heading, `doc §n`, `path:line`, `path:a-b` or `path#Heading` | `get "prd §4.2"` |
    26	| Wording or a paraphrase | `search <words>`, then `get` the top hit's reference (`--expand 1` inlines it) |
    27	| "All" or "every" place citing X | `refs FR-12`: includes lines inside ranges such as FR-9–FR-12; `--children` adds FR-12.k, `--kind binds` narrows |
    28	| The shape of a document | `outline [file] --level 2` |
    29	| A change to review | `diff <old-rev> [<new-rev>]` (default new: the worktree; flags shifted FR-n.k lists and added IDs already in the file's history), then `impact <ID or path:a-b>`, then `lint` |
    30	| Tickets | `covers` checks every ticket's covers chain; `coverage --by tickets\|architecture\|ux [--only gaps]` |
    31	| Whether specdex can be trusted here | `status` |
    32	
    33	One unit answers what it says, not what other units add. When the question is about a concept other rules may also constrain (who owns something, a limit, an exception, whether something exists at all), also `search` the concept's key term before answering, and say which units you checked.
    34	
    35	`get` takes several references in one call; `--budget N` caps output in tokens but never cuts a single unit. Paths are project-relative; cite them exactly as printed. `get` and `refs` also accept any unique path suffix.
    36	
    37	`--scope` chooses which files count: `record` (default) is the specs of record; `current` adds rationale and tickets; `rationale`, `trail`, `memlog` and `all` reach the history. Stay on the default unless the question is about why or when something was decided.
    38	
    39	## Read the output
    40	
    41	Each hit starts `path:start-end [labels] — heading path`. Labels read `[role; temporal; decision: ...; flags; authority]`, with the parts that apply:
    42	
    43	- **role**: `record` is the current spec of record, the only text that states current requirements. `ambiguous` is one of several candidate documents of one type with no overlay choice between them. `rationale` explains current decisions but requires nothing. `ticket`, `noncurrent` (an older document of a type that was not selected), `trail` (reviews, drafts, discussions), `memlog` and `unverified` (no rule matched) are not current requirements.
    44	- **historical**: text kept as history inside a record, such as declined proposals, retired claims, or change requests as raised. It is true about the past, not about now.
    45	- **decision: X**: on a change-request row, the decision taken. The decision is current; the request text is not.
    46	- **flags** such as `assumption`, `note-for-pm`, `non-goal`, `conditional`: the unit is provisional or deliberately out of scope; say so when citing it.
    47	- **superseded by prd [except ...]**: the PRD wins over this file, except in the named sections, which show `authoritative exception (...)`.
    48	
    49	Quote only `record` text without `historical` as a current requirement, and cite it as `path:start-end` with its labels.
    50	
    51	Statuses in `resolve`, `refs`, `impact` and `lint`:
    52	
    53	- `defined`: exactly one definition.
    54	- `ambiguous`: several definitions or candidate documents. Do not pick one; report them. When the definitions sit in different document scopes (AD in two spines, CAP in two specs), the citing document decides; otherwise suggest choosing the record in the overlay's `[current] records`.
    55	- `out-of-bounds`: a positional ID past the end of its list (FR-12.9 when FR-12 has 5 items); the note gives the count.
    56	- `not defined` or `unresolved`: a dangling reference.
    57	- `elaborated only`: elaborated somewhere but not defined in its owner document.
    58	- `textual`: a phrase such as "all MVP FRs" may bind the ID; read the line to decide.
    59	
    60	An empty answer says `none in a fully indexed scope`, which is a real negative, or `unknown (...)`, which is not: part of the scope could not be indexed. Every output ends with `generation <hash>`, the verified index state the answer came from.
    61	
    62	`lint` is mechanical: duplicates, dangling or out-of-range references, unknown tokens, missing companions, replica drift, and BMAD's own spine validator. Its last lines say what it did not check: a clean lint does not mean the specs agree, and contradictions in meaning still need reading.
    63	
    64	## Exit codes
    65	
    66	| Code | Meaning |
    67	|---|---|
    68	| 0 | Done |
    69	| 1 | Findings: `resolve` not `defined`, `lint` high severity, `coverage` gaps, `covers` problems |
    70	| 2 | Usage error, unknown reference or scope, or the files kept changing during the call |
    71	| 3 | Configuration or source error: unreadable profile or overlay, unreadable git revision |
    72	
    73	## When to fall back
    74	
    75	Say that specdex could not answer and use `rg -n` over the output folder (usually `_bmad-output/`) plus bounded reads of the matching section when:
    76	
    77	- it exits 3;
    78	- `status` shows `diagnostic unsupported-layout` (sharded v6 `index.md`, initiative-v7 folders) or `ambiguous-current`;
    79	- `status` shows no `record` files: specdex found no specs where the profile looks, so its negatives mean nothing;
    80	- an empty answer is `unknown (...)`;
    81	- `search` misses a paraphrase after one retry with other words.
    82	
    83	`status` showing `profile ... (unverified)` means the installed BMAD differs from the version the profile was built for; results still come, but check surprising ones by reading.
    84	
    85	## Read-only
    86	
    87	specdex never writes inside the project; its index lives in the user cache, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/specdex/` (default `$HOME/.cache/specdex/`), or at `--db`. It reports evidence; changing a spec is the owning BMAD skill's job: `bmad-prd` for the PRD and addendum, `bmad-ux` for DESIGN.md and EXPERIENCE.md, `bmad-architecture` for the spine, `bmad-spec` for specs, `bmad-preview-ticketing` for tickets, `bmad-correct-course` for a change across documents. After such an edit, `impact` and `lint` show what else needs attention. The overlay is the project's configuration; edit it only when the user asks.

All published pass decisions reproduce. The conclusions are narrower than universal integrity/freshness.

| Cases | Established by control/detection | Limit / possible wrong-reason pass |
|---|---|---|
| B01 | New short-range citing line appears in refs and impact. | No long/positional/invalid ranges. |
| B02–B03 | Specific deletion shifts cited FR-88.3; specific edit reports FR-88.4 only. | Counts/new text not fully asserted; no scoped collisions/complex list combinations. |
| B04 | Same-folder CAP mentions resolve; outside README is ambiguous. | No explicit cross-folder citations or third namespace. |
| B05 | Sole upstream AD resolves; local redefinition flags inherited conflict. | No competing parents; does not prove From-parent field determines target. |
| B06–B07 | Missing companion/absent local E9 flagged against clean controls. | No ambiguous upstream or ownership-bypass case. |
| B08 | File/entry disagreement detected. | Does not assert file coverage wins or inspect exit status. |

| B12 | Copied PRD repeating FR-71 causes ambiguity. | Unique IDs in candidates remain falsely defined. |

| F5 | Sequential branch switch and commit lookup see expected keyword. | No branch change during inventory/query. |
| F6 | Two post-edit status processes return one generation. | Control is unconditionally true; no interleaving writer/reader across commits. |
